title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Kyklaminos root has route-conditioned reproductive effects, with wearer co-reference unpaid
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the complete critical-text paragraph II.164 §1, Dioscorides attributes to report (“they say”) that if a pregnant woman steps across the root, she miscarries; the next clause calls it an oxytocic when worn. C0 source-model: the same named Kyklaminos root participates in two distinct bodily relations—stepped over under the explicit pregnancy condition versus worn as an amulet—with opposite reproductive outcomes. Do not rewrite this as one static harmful/helpful property. The second clause does not explicitly name its wearer; treating the wearer as that same pregnant woman is a paid, unresolved co-reference, not a fact. The rest of §1 still has separate oral/topical menstrual effects, poison-antidote claims, and wine-induced intoxication; this candidate does not collapse them into the pair. Retained layer is Wellmann’s 1907–14 critical text, not a complete medieval transcript: Morgan M.652 f72v contains the beginning only, and f73r was not acquired. No Voynich whole form or target binding was accessed. A later C0 reading would have to preserve one root, a conditional patient relation, hearsay attribution, and the wearing/step contrast; otherwise reject.

design.mechanism: Separate outcome by relation-to-agent and scope the pregnancy condition locally: crossing over the root while pregnant is reported to cause miscarriage; wearing the root is separately said to hasten childbirth. A broad plant-name/default-efficacy reading cannot absorb these as one unconditional property.
design.unit: The entire Greek text block labelled II.164, Section 1 in H_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md, not a favorable clause crop. Its scope includes morphology and root-drink menstrual action; oral and topical venom-antidote routes; the wine-mixture intoxication claim; the conditional crossing/wearing contrast. Source is the retained Wellmann XML critical-edition cache, 1907–1914. It is an ancient text in modern critical edition, not a diplomatic reading of Morgan M.652. The dossier says the f72v local witness has image/synonym/opening description and continuation; it explicitly does not verify this section-1 clause pair in the medieval witness.
design.contrast: Conditional, route-indexed opposition (pregnant woman crosses root → reported miscarriage; root worn → birth-accelerating property) versus one global harmful or beneficial root gloss, or versus an unlicensed claim that the same woman fills both roles.
design.prediction: Any future already-authorized whole reading using this source model must keep the named root as the shared candidate referent, preserve “they say” as attribution, attach pregnancy to the step-over event, and represent the worn-root use separately. It must either leave wearer identity open or explicitly pay for same-woman co-reference. It must leave §1’s other oral/topical/poison/wine branches distinct. If one route or one unconditioned root adjective is required to explain both reproductive outcomes, the proposal fails.
design.scope: Raw C0 source-model only: no Voynich exact word or group selected, no target data opened, no target result claimed. New provisional content values: ROOT=Kyklaminos root; CROSSING-OVER relation; condition=PREGNANT; outcome=MISCARRIAGE (reported); WEARING relation; outcome=CHILDBIRTH-ACCELERATION. Paid unresolved choice: whether wearer=the explicitly mentioned pregnant woman. Other Section-1 event branches remain open. Modern drug-safety interpretation is out of scope.
design.predecessors_and_counterexamples: Nearby but distinct predecessor IDEA667 models one plant as hazardous at collection/protected in mixture; IDEA601 tracks dependency roles in a different complete source; IDEA344 is a generic condition-guard model with a missing complete-target contract. GDT568 shows owner/action frames can be rendered in a workshop lexicon, not that this source model maps to a Voynich frame. GDT608 retains atomic whole-form advantage; GDT326 is a counterexample to freely predicting unseen combinations. These are dependencies/limits, not evidence of source-to-target identity.

source_evidence.quote: φασὶ δὲ ὅτι, κἂν ὑπερβῇ τὴν ῥίζαν ἐγκύμων γυνή, ἐξαμβλώσκειν αὐτήν· ἔστι δὲ καὶ ὠκυτόκιον περιαπτομένη.
